stem: Besides infections of the reproductive system, gastrointestinal tract, and other body areas, metronidazole is also used to treat which group of diseases?

options.label: A
options.misconception: None — metronidazole also treats certain STDs, alongside infections at many body sites.
options.explanation: The label says metronidazole treats infections of the reproductive system, GI tract, skin and many other areas, and is also used for certain sexually transmitted diseases.

options.label: B
options.misconception: Assumes a broad antimicrobial also covers viruses.
options.explanation: Viral respiratory diseases such as influenza are treated with antivirals such as oseltamivir; metronidazole has no antiviral activity.

options.label: C
options.misconception: Assumes a drug used for skin infections also covers fungal ones.
options.explanation: Fungal skin diseases such as ringworm are treated with azole or allylamine antifungals; metronidazole does not act on fungi.

options.label: D
options.misconception: Confuses antiprotozoal activity with activity against parasitic worms.
options.explanation: Intestinal worm infections such as pinworm are treated with anthelmintics such as albendazole; metronidazole is not an anthelmintic.

options.label: E
options.misconception: Assumes an antibacterial used for lung infections also covers mycobacteria.
options.explanation: Mycobacterial lung diseases such as tuberculosis need multidrug regimens built on isoniazid and rifampin; metronidazole is not used.

context: Learning objective: Metronidazole treats infections of the reproductive system, GI tract, and many other body areas, plus certain sexually transmitted diseases.
